image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A small sore can form on the soft lining inside the mouth. Many causes are possible, and a clinician can help assess a sore that does not heal.
common_symptoms: A round or oval sore inside the mouth
Soreness when eating or speaking
risk_factors: Mouth irritation or accidental biting
Stress or some health conditions
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush gently twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
Avoid foods that irritate a sore and keep the mouth clean.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a doctor or dentist if a sore lasts more than 2 weeks, keeps returning, or makes eating difficult.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A white patch may appear on the lining of the mouth. Only a qualified clinician can assess what is causing it.
common_symptoms: A white patch that does not rub away
A patch that may feel rough or thick
risk_factors: Tobacco, gutkha, or areca nut use
Long-term irritation inside the mouth
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid tobacco, gutkha, and areca nut; ask a health worker about support.
Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and attend regular dental checks.
when_to_consult_doctor: Any white patch or non-healing ulcer lasting more than 2 weeks needs a doctor visit.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A persistent red patch can occur on the mouth lining. It needs professional assessment and cannot be identified from appearance alone.
common_symptoms: A red area that remains on the mouth lining
A smooth or velvety-looking patch
risk_factors: Tobacco, gutkha, or areca nut use
Long-term irritation of the mouth
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid tobacco, gutkha, and areca nut and seek help to stop.
Keep regular dental check-ups and brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
when_to_consult_doctor: Any red patch or non-healing ulcer lasting more than 2 weeks needs a doctor visit.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: This condition can make the inside of the mouth feel tight and make opening the mouth harder. A doctor or dentist should assess these changes.
common_symptoms: Tightness or burning in the mouth
Difficulty opening the mouth or eating spicy food
risk_factors: Areca nut, betel quid, or gutkha use
Use of products that contain areca nut
prevention_and_hygiene: Stop areca nut, gutkha, and tobacco use; ask a health worker for support.
Attend regular dental checks and keep the mouth clean.
when_to_consult_doctor: Arrange a doctor visit for mouth tightness or reduced opening. Any non-healing ulcer or white/red patch lasting more than 2 weeks also needs a doctor visit.

clinical_photo.credit: Luca Pastore, Maria Luisa Fiorella, Raffaele Fiorella, Lorenzo Lo Muzio

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Cancer can affect parts of the mouth. A sore, lump, or patch can have many causes; only a qualified clinician can assess it.
common_symptoms: A sore, lump, or patch that does not heal
Trouble chewing, swallowing, or moving the tongue
risk_factors: Tobacco, gutkha, or areca nut use
Heavy alcohol use can add to risk
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid tobacco, gutkha, and areca nut; ask for help to stop.
Attend regular mouth checks and brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
when_to_consult_doctor: Any non-healing ulcer or white/red patch lasting more than 2 weeks needs a doctor visit. Seek prompt care for a new lump or difficulty swallowing.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Gingivitis is irritation and swelling of the gums, often linked with plaque around the teeth.
common_symptoms: Red or puffy gums
Gums that bleed during brushing
risk_factors: Plaque left on teeth
Smoking or difficulty cleaning between teeth
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and clean between teeth.
Visit a dentist regularly for advice on gum care.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a dentist if bleeding or swelling continues, or if you have pain or loose teeth.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Long-lasting gum inflammation can affect the tissues that hold teeth in place. A dentist can check gum health.
common_symptoms: Gums that bleed or pull away from teeth
Bad breath or teeth that feel loose
risk_factors: Untreated gum inflammation
Tobacco use or some long-term health conditions
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and clean between teeth.
Avoid tobacco and keep regular dental appointments.
when_to_consult_doctor: Arrange a dental visit for ongoing bleeding, gum changes, or any loose tooth.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Tooth decay damages the hard outer part of a tooth. Early changes may not hurt, so regular dental checks matter.
common_symptoms: Tooth sensitivity or pain
A visible spot or hole in a tooth
risk_factors: Frequent sugary food or drinks
Not brushing regularly with fluoride toothpaste
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
Limit sugary snacks and drinks and attend regular dental checks.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a dentist for tooth pain, sensitivity, or a visible change in a tooth.

clinical_photo.credit: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Oral thrush is a yeast overgrowth in the mouth. A clinician can assess mouth changes and decide what care is needed.
common_symptoms: Creamy-looking areas on the tongue or cheeks
Soreness or an altered taste
risk_factors: Some medicines or health conditions
Dry mouth or dentures that do not fit well
prevention_and_hygiene: Clean teeth and dentures every day.
Drink water and ask a clinician about ongoing mouth dryness.
when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a clinician for white areas, mouth soreness, or trouble swallowing, especially if symptoms persist.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Some tongues have smooth patches that change shape or place over time. A dentist can check if a tongue change needs attention.
common_symptoms: Smooth red patches with pale borders
Patches that may move over days or weeks
risk_factors: The cause is not always known
Some people notice irritation from certain foods
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush teeth and tongue gently.
Avoid foods that cause irritation and drink enough water.
when_to_consult_doctor: Ask a dentist about a new or painful tongue change, or if it does not improve.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: This long-term inflammatory condition can affect the lining of the mouth. It is not something a person can confirm by looking at it.
common_symptoms: Fine white lines or sore areas inside the cheeks
Burning or discomfort with some foods
risk_factors: The exact cause may not be clear
Some medicines or immune responses may be linked
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush gently twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
Avoid tobacco and keep regular dental appointments.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a dentist or doctor for mouth sores, persistent burning, or any lasting change.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A dental abscess is a pocket of infection near a tooth or gum. It needs timely assessment by a dentist.
common_symptoms: Strong tooth or gum pain
Swelling, bad taste, or fever
risk_factors: Untreated tooth decay
A cracked tooth or gum disease
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and attend dental checks.
Seek dental care early for tooth pain.
when_to_consult_doctor: Contact a dentist promptly for swelling or severe tooth pain. Seek urgent care for facial swelling, fever, or trouble breathing or swallowing.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Cold sores are small blisters, often on or near the lips. They are commonly linked to a virus and can spread through close contact.
common_symptoms: Tingling or itching near the lips
Small grouped blisters that later form a crust
risk_factors: Close contact with an active sore
Illness, stress, or sunlight may trigger a return
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid sharing cups, towels, or lip products during an outbreak.
Wash hands after touching the area and avoid touching the eyes.
when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a clinician if sores are severe, often return, affect the eyes, or do not heal.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A lasting burning feeling in the mouth can have many causes. A clinician can check for possible reasons and support next steps.
common_symptoms: Burning or tingling of the tongue or mouth
Dry mouth or a changed taste
risk_factors: Dry mouth or some medicines
Some health or nutrition conditions
prevention_and_hygiene: Drink water and use a soft toothbrush.
Tell a clinician about medicines and other symptoms; do not stop prescribed medicines on your own.
when_to_consult_doctor: Arrange a doctor or dentist visit if burning continues or affects eating, drinking, or sleep.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Candida is a yeast that can sometimes grow too much in the mouth. A clinician can assess symptoms and decide what they mean.
common_symptoms: Sore mouth or white-looking areas
A changed taste or discomfort while eating
risk_factors: Some medicines or health conditions
Dry mouth or dentures
prevention_and_hygiene: Clean teeth and dentures daily and brush gently.
Ask a clinician for advice if mouth dryness or soreness continues.
when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a clinician for persistent white areas, soreness, or difficulty swallowing.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: PVL is a term for white patches that may grow or return over time. A specialist clinician must assess persistent patches.
common_symptoms: One or more white patches in the mouth
Patches that slowly spread or return
risk_factors: The cause is not fully understood
It can occur even without tobacco use
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid tobacco, gutkha, and areca nut.
Keep scheduled dental or specialist follow-up and brush gently.
when_to_consult_doctor: Any non-healing ulcer or white/red patch lasting more than 2 weeks needs a doctor visit.

clinical_photo.credit: Victoria Kuta and S. Mark Taylor

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Long-term sun exposure can make the lips dry or rough. A health professional can check lasting lip changes.
common_symptoms: Dry, rough, or cracked areas on the lip
A change in the lip border or colour
risk_factors: Long periods in strong sunlight
Outdoor work without lip or skin sun protection
prevention_and_hygiene: Use shade and suitable sun protection for the lips.
Avoid tobacco and attend regular dental or medical checks.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a doctor for a lasting lip sore or changing patch, especially one that does not heal.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: These are irritated areas in the mouth that can look like other conditions. A clinician can review possible causes.
common_symptoms: White lines or red sore areas
Burning or discomfort in one part of the mouth
risk_factors: Some medicines or dental materials
The cause may not be clear
prevention_and_hygiene: Keep teeth clean and attend regular dental visits.
Tell a clinician about medicines; do not stop them without advice.
when_to_consult_doctor: Ask a dentist or doctor to assess a lasting sore, patch, or mouth irritation.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Lupus can sometimes affect the mouth. A clinician should assess mouth sores, especially alongside other health changes.
common_symptoms: Sore areas or red patches in the mouth
Mouth dryness or discomfort
risk_factors: A person’s immune system and health history
Some medicines or illness can affect symptoms
prevention_and_hygiene: Brush gently twice daily and keep regular medical and dental visits.
Tell the care team about new mouth changes and medicines.
when_to_consult_doctor: Contact a doctor if mouth sores persist, worsen, or occur with other new symptoms.

name_hi: बिना धुएँ वाले तंबाकू से केराटोसिस
image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Tobacco kept in the mouth can irritate the nearby lining and cause a pale or thick area. A clinician should assess lasting changes.
common_symptoms: A pale, thick, or wrinkled area where tobacco is placed
Mouth irritation
risk_factors: Chewing or holding tobacco, gutkha, or related products in the mouth
prevention_and_hygiene: Stop smokeless tobacco and ask a health worker for help.
Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste and keep regular dental visits.
when_to_consult_doctor: Any non-healing ulcer or white/red patch lasting more than 2 weeks needs a doctor visit.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: A lasting white, ridged area can form on the side of the tongue. A health professional should assess this change.
common_symptoms: White ridged or folded-looking area on the tongue
Usually little or no pain
risk_factors: Some immune system conditions
Certain viral infections
prevention_and_hygiene: Keep regular medical and dental check-ups.
Brush gently and tell a clinician about new mouth changes.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a clinician for any white tongue patch that remains or changes.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: The corners of the mouth can become sore or cracked. Dryness and other causes may play a part.
common_symptoms: Cracks or redness at one or both mouth corners
Soreness when opening the mouth
risk_factors: Saliva or moisture collecting at the corners
Dry lips, dentures, or some health conditions
prevention_and_hygiene: Keep the area clean and avoid repeatedly licking the lips.
Drink water and ask a clinician if cracks keep returning.
when_to_consult_doctor: See a clinician if the corners do not heal, are very painful, or keep cracking.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Dry mouth means there is not enough saliva to keep the mouth comfortable. It can affect speaking, eating, and teeth.
common_symptoms: A dry or sticky feeling
Difficulty swallowing dry food or speaking for long
risk_factors: Some medicines or health conditions
Not drinking enough water or tobacco use
prevention_and_hygiene: Sip water often and brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.
Ask a clinician to review ongoing dryness and medicines.
when_to_consult_doctor: Talk with a doctor or dentist if dryness lasts or makes eating, speaking, or swallowing difficult.

image_credit: Original, non-graphic educational illustration created for Aarogya Drishti.
short_description: Oral herpes is caused by a common virus and may cause sores around the mouth. A clinician can advise about symptoms and spread.
common_symptoms: Tingling followed by small blisters or sores
Sores that may crust as they heal
risk_factors: Close contact with an active sore
Illness or stress may be linked with a return
prevention_and_hygiene: Avoid kissing or sharing items that touch the mouth during an outbreak.
Wash hands after touching a sore and avoid touching the eyes.
when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a clinician for severe, frequent, or slow-healing sores, or sores near the eyes.
